investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T03:31:06Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The swarm backend rejected the agent creation request before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be collected, causing a total contract gap across all four required evidence fields.
investigation.rootCause: The eval service account's organization has reached the swarm backend's hard agent quota limit of 100. When the eval runner called POST /api/agents (via createAgent in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 791), the swarm layer returned a 409 conflict response with the nested error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because agent creation failed immediately, no agent was provisioned, no VM was assigned, and no evidence could be written — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production API; no evidence of user-traffic impact or a production incident is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): The eval service account's org has accumulated 100 or more remote agents that were not cleaned up by prior eval runs (e.g., withCleanup failed or was skipped), exhausting the swarm quota and blocking all new agent creation attempts.
Secondary (medium confidence): A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before the cleanup phase, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota without being deleted.
Tertiary (low confidence): The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a backend configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to suddenly hit the ceiling.

Low confidence hypothesis: Commit aee54ab ('ci(observability): guard release history publishing') touched workflow files including .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-observability-repair.yml; if a workflow change inadvertently disabled the cleanup/repair step, orphaned agents could accumulate. investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" for every POST /api/agents call issued by the observability probe org. The root cause is a quota exhaustion condition on the probe org's swarm agent slot, not a code defect in the eval runner itself.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable (SESSION_OPEN_FAILED / 404)
investigation.summary: The eval check `image-generation-stream` failed because the SSE stream to `/api/generate/image/stream` received a `generation_error` frame with code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and an HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness was unreachable or misconfigured at the time of the run. As a direct consequence, the stream never progressed past `generation_start`, so neither required evidence key (`frameTypes` containing `generation_completed`, nor `imageUrlPresent`) was produced, causing the contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime endpoint targeted by the eval harness returned HTTP 404 during the `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error, meaning the harness was either not deployed, deployed at a different URL than configured in `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, or running an incompatible version that no longer exposes the expected route. This is an eval infrastructure / harness connectivity failure localized to the `image-generation-stream` check and the `/api/generate/image/stream` endpoint. No sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so this is scoped to the eval run and does not confirm a production user-facing outage.
